articles.title: [Editorial] Multiple sclerosis: beyond controlling relapses
articles.author: The Lancet
articles.summary: Few neurological diseases have seen a transformation in diagnosis and treatment as remarkable as multiple sclerosis. A chronic, heterogeneous autoimmune condition, it typically begins in early adulthood and affects over 3 million people, with women roughly three times more likely to be affected than men.

articles.title: New gum disease treatment kills bad bacteria while sparing the good
articles.summary: Researchers in Japan have developed an innovative gum disease treatment that uses egg yolk antibodies and near-infrared light to destroy harmful bacteria without harming beneficial microbes. Unlike conventional treatments, the approach preserves the mouth's natural bacterial balance and protects healthy gum cells.

articles.title: Mysterious new viruses reveal a missing link in evolution
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered previously unknown viruses that could help explain how some of life’s earliest biological structures evolved. The surprising findings challenge a longstanding evolutionary theory and suggest that viruses may have hidden capabilities far beyond simply infecting cells.

articles.title: Scientists discover that leukemia can begin developing 50 years before diagnosis
articles.summary: A groundbreaking study reveals that acute myeloid leukemia (AML), an aggressive blood cancer, can begin developing more than 50 years before diagnosis, with the first cancer-driving mutation appearing before age 20 in two-thirds of cases.

articles.title: FDA Approves First Drug to Treat Neurological Symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher Disease
articles.author: FDA
articles.summary: FDA today approved Infilbray (venglustat) tablets, the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher disease (GD3) in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kg (approximately 33 pounds).
